body.name: Positive Fourier minimum-distance estimator
body.construction:
For every \(a\in\mathcal A\), put \(\eta_N=N^{-1}\), \(s_L^a(y)=\operatorname{Re}\sum_{\|\ell\|_\infty\le L_N}\widehat c_{a\ell}e^{\mathrm i\ell^\top y}\), \(g_L^a(y)=\max\{\eta_N,s_L^a(y)\}\), and
\[
\widehat p_L^a(y)=\eta_N+(1-\eta_N)\frac{g_L^a(y)}{\int g_L^a d\lambda^n}.
\]
This density integrates to one and is everywhere at least \(\eta_N\); unlike mixing with a fixed positive constant, the added uniform mass vanishes. Put \(\widehat{\mathbb P}_L=(\widehat p_L^a d\lambda^n:a\in\mathcal A)\). Let \(\mathfrak M_N\) be a finite subset of \(\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\), supplied together with certificates of membership, whose induced complete observed-law families form a \(\delta_N\)-net in complete-family Hellinger distance. Close \(\mathfrak M_N\) under the finite set of common node relabelings. Such finite nets exist because the induced observed densities have a common \(C^{s_{\mathrm{obs}}}\) bound and hence their finite-family image is totally bounded in \(L^2\) and Hellinger distance. Define \(\widehat\theta_N\in\mathfrak M_N\) to satisfy
\[
\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}H^2(P_{\widehat\theta_N}^a,\widehat p_L^a d\lambda^n)\right\}^{1/2}
\le
\min_{\vartheta\in\mathfrak M_N}
\left\{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}H^2(P_\vartheta^a,\widehat p_L^a d\lambda^n)\right\}^{1/2}+\delta_N.
\]
The optimization variables are the finitely many certified models \(\vartheta\in\mathfrak M_N\), and the displayed finite-family Hellinger criterion is the objective.
